name: Jade Plant
hook: Leaves dropping? Your jade is probably overwatered.

steps.title: 4+ hours of direct sun
steps.tip: A south window is ideal. Too little light gives dark, droopy growth without red leaf edges.

steps.title: Let it dry out fully
steps.tip: Water deeply only once the soil is completely dry, and less in winter. Wet soil causes leaf drop and rot.

steps.title: Gritty mix, clay pot
steps.tip: Use cactus or succulent mix in a pot with a drainage hole; terracotta dries out faster than plastic.

steps.title: Warm days, cool nights
steps.tip: Best at 18–24°C by day and 10–13°C at night. Keep leaves off cold windowpanes in winter.

steps.title: Feed lightly
steps.tip: A balanced liquid feed 2–3 times in spring and summer. Too much fertilizer makes it leggy.

steps.title: Swab off mealybugs
steps.tip: Dab white, fluffy mealybugs with rubbing alcohol on a cotton swab. Skip insecticidal soap.

outro: Lots of sun and a dry spell between drinks keep a jade happy.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture Extension: Jade Plant, Crassula ovata
Penn State Extension: Jade Plant, A No Fuss Houseplant
ASPCA: Jade Plant (listed as Crassula argentea)

faqs.question: What are the tiny white or black dots on the leaves?
faqs.answer: They're normal. The dots are hydathodes, pores the plant uses to move water, not a disease or a pest.
